long_biography.plain_text:
At the post office in Split, Juroslav Buljubašić learned to install and repair telephone exchanges. In 1984 he left with five colleagues to form SEM, offering technical work at prices below state competitors. Cable and satellite television followed, giving him the capital and confidence to move into engineering, banking, hotels, renewable energy and commercial shipping.

Buljubašić preferred partnerships and minority positions to a conventional holding company. He founded businesses, placed managers in charge and sold or reduced stakes as opportunities changed. By the end of his operating career, he had exited most Croatian companies and redirected capital into shares across dozens of international businesses. That transition made marketable investments the clearest final form of a fortune he had first built through entrepreneurship.

uncertainties.detail: Reliable profiles establish Split and 1960 as the birthplace and year, but no strong public source found in this pass gives a birth day or month. Reports variously say he died in his 63rd or 64th year, so no exact death age is proposed.

Detailed 2017 interviews establish that Buljubašić had sold or transferred most operating companies and held shares across dozens of international businesses. Public obituaries in 2023 do not enumerate the estate or confirm every position still held at death, so individual securities, fund stakes and former operating assets are not listed as final personal holdings.

Founder best describes how Buljubašić created his wealth through SEM and subsequent ventures. Investor best describes the last documented structure of that wealth after he reduced or sold operating stakes and shifted into funds and public-company shares.

Historical fleets, hotels, bank assets, wind-energy facilities, company revenue and the combined assets of partners or family members are not treated as Buljubašić's personal wealth. Only directly documented equity and sale or investment activity informs the classifications.

No dedicated Forbes profile was found. No personal social-media account or website met the verification threshold, and a reported announcement on a Facebook page did not expose a sufficiently verified profile URL for proposal.
Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sanctions, irrelevant private-family detail and all private-vessel research were excluded.
